## Overview

Add opt-in tensor-parallel sharding of the MiniMax M3 FP8 indexer cache. On supported TP4 Blackwell deployments, each rank stores one quarter of the token rows in every index-K page and exchanges partial block maxima for the existing Top-K selection.

## Claims

- Reduce persistent index-K bytes per block per rank by 75%, with separate symmetric receive/staging buffer overhead. Main attention Q/K/V partitioning and cache precision are unchanged.
- Support decode, CUDA Graph replay, and prefill reconstruction through the MSA backend, behind `--attention-config '{"indexer_cache_sharding":"on","indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'`. The default is `off`; `auto` applies backend-specific eligibility and workload thresholds.
- Coordinate catchable rank-local allocation failures and prefill-gather kernel compilation/loading failures before the corresponding peer rendezvous, so ranks select the same fallback instead of entering different collectives.

## Validation

Validated commit `f2f35b3785` (parent `de7d70676d`) on four GB200 GPUs:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Saved pre-fix initialization + rank-1 receive-allocation failure | Reproduced the hang: peers blocked in rendezvous while the failing rank entered the fallback CPU all-reduce. The 90-second watchdog terminated the test. |
| Fixed TP4 integration and three injected initialization failures | Passed, 149.10 seconds. |
| MSA/CuTe baseline, sharded score, packed-cache layout, and FP8 insertion | 30 passed, 198.53 seconds. |
| Full M3 checkpoint, sharding off/on with matched FlashInfer tactics | 1,024 generated tokens matched exactly; maximum absolute difference across 5,120 paired top-5 logprobs was 0. See the numerical control below. |

```bash
cd /work/source
export PYTHONPATH=/work/source OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MAX_JOBS=8
/work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_minimax_m3_indexer_sharding.py -v -s
/work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py \
  -k 'sharded_decode_index_score or indexer_cache_squeezes or fmha_sm100_indexer_matches_reference or decode_index_score_cutedsl_correctness or sparse_full_fp8_index' -v
```

All changed-file pre-commit checks passed. Runtime: PyTorch `2.15.0a0+875d815502.nvinternal.main`, CUDA 13.5, CUTLASS DSL 4.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2rc4, and Ray 2.56.1. Official ARM64 wheel extensions from `9b99ccb56` were used after verifying that all compiled-source/build paths match the tested commit; no operator replacement was used.

<details>
<summary>Full-model E2E setup and numerical control</summary>

Loaded the complete `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` checkpoint at revision `901464083161bf8612a29ff7ad29914cd4ab4a85`. Settings: TP4, BF16 activations, FP8 index cache, 128-token pages, 16,384 maximum model length, 8 maximum sequences, 2,048 batched tokens, 4 GiB KV-cache budget per rank, chunked prefill and prefix caching enabled, and full decode CUDA Graphs captured at sizes 1/2/4/8. Each request generated 64 greedy tokens with raw top-5 logprobs. No speculative decoding was used.

| Workload | Compared generated tokens | Token mismatches | Max absolute logprob difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sequential prompts of 128, 2,304, and 8,192 tokens, each repeated twice with prefix cache reset | 384 | 0 | 0 |
| Mixed batch of 8 prompts, spanning 128 to 8,192 tokens | 512 | 0 | 0 |
| Two requests reusing cached prefixes | 128 | 0 | 0 |

Both modes also reproduced their sequential outputs exactly across repeats. The compared mixed and prefix-reuse runs had matching dispatch signatures, exercised mixed prefill/decode and full CUDA Graph replay, and completed with the one-sided page gather enabled on all four sharded ranks.

**Numerical control:** Independently autotuned off/on runs did not meet the exact-output criterion. Replicating index-Q changes the combined QKV projection width from 2,560 to 2,944; FlashInfer selected different GEMM tactics, including split-K counts. Matching common GEMM/MoE tactics alone still left 115/192 sequential tokens different. Matching the shape-specific QKV split-K count as well (4 for both widths at decode batch sizes 1/2/4/8) produced the results above. Every rank loaded the same 144-entry controlled tactic cache; the caches were unchanged after execution, with no retuning logged. These are finite-workload equivalence results under matched tactics, not a guarantee of exact outputs with independent autotuning or a model-quality evaluation. Tactic-cache controls are test setup only and are not added to production code.

Worker inspection confirmed index pages changed from `[882, 128, 128]` to `[1031, 32, 128]`, reducing index-K storage from 16 KiB to 4 KiB per page per rank. Under the fixed KV budget, total token capacity increased from 112,896 to 131,968. This excludes additional replicated projection weights and symmetric buffers (3 MiB receive plus two 64 MiB staging buffers per rank in this run). No E2E speedup is claimed.

`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` was used in both modes because the existing prefill planner performs a CPU transfer; this is not a strict sync-free validation.

</details>

The committed tests extend the existing M3 score/cache-insert suites and add one manual four-GPU test for production MSA dispatch. The TP4 test exercises DQL 1/4/8, multiple layers, mailbox reuse, CUDA Graph replay, mixed prefill/decode, shared pages, one-sided and NCCL page reconstruction, and rank-local initialization failures. No CI jobs are added or changed; TP4 symmetric-memory coverage requires four peer-accessible SM100-family GPUs and is documented in the existing manual-test allowlist.

## Details

Rank `r` owns token rows `r, r+4, ...` within each 128-token page, retaining all 128 index-K dimensions for each owned token. All index-Q heads are projected locally. The score kernel sends partial block maxima to each head's owner, which reduces them before existing Top-K selection. Prefill reconstructs full pages using symmetric staging, with NCCL fallback.

Eligibility is limited to TP4, SM100-family GPUs, FP8 index cache, MSA top-16, supported speculative methods with index-head count times maximum query length at most 32, and no prefill/decode context parallelism. Unsupported deployments retain replicated storage. Query replication and communication add work; shorter contexts may be slower. The change keeps the upstream prefill planner.

Initialization coordinates each local preparation phase over the TP CPU group before its corresponding peer rendezvous. Receive-buffer allocation/initialization is coordinated first; page-gather allocation and kernel compilation/loading are coordinated before the later staging-buffer rendezvous. This handles catchable local setup failures; process death or communication-internal failures remain engine errors. Decode kernels compile during the normal warmup path.

Related work: [#59980](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59980) retains replicated index-K storage and distributes whole-block scoring, with query and Top-K candidate gathers. [#57909](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57909) implements AMD block-scoring CP and shares the replicated index-Q loader mechanism; that loader support should be reused when either change lands. This PR changes physical token-row ownership and reconstructs pages for prefill. [#59979](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59979) separately changes prefill planning.

Adapted from Suyog Gupta's [index-K sharding commit](https://github.com/xinli-sw/vllm/commit/69a7c7bf290843181349fc958b10f902276e7b09), with backend integration, reduced scope, initialization coordination, and tests. AI assistance was used for extraction, implementation, review, and validation.

@@ -0,0 +1,291 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import faulthandler
+
+import pytest
+import ray
+import torch
+
+from tests.v1.attention.utils import (
+    BatchSpec,
+    create_common_attn_metadata,
+    create_vllm_config,
+)
+from vllm.config import SpeculativeConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.forward_context import set_forward_context
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+from ..utils import init_test_distributed_environment, multi_process_parallel
+
+
+@ray.remote(num_gpus=1, max_calls=1)
+def _indexer_sharding(monkeypatch, tp_size, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port):
+    from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_tp_group
+    from vllm.models.minimax_m3.nvidia import indexer_msa as msa
+
+    with monkeypatch.context() as m:
+        m.delenv("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", raising=False)
+        device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}")
+        torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+        config = create_vllm_config(
+            model_name="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
+            tensor_parallel_size=tp_size,
+            block_size=128,
+            max_model_len=4096,
+            max_num_seqs=4,
+            max_num_batched_tokens=256,
+            hf_config_override={
+                "sparse_attention_config": {
+                    "sparse_num_index_heads": 4,
+                    "sparse_index_dim": 128,
+                }
+            },
+        )
+        config.speculative_config = SpeculativeConfig(
+            method="ngram", num_speculative_tokens=7
+        )
+        config.attention_config.indexer_cache_sharding = "on"
+        with set_current_vllm_config(config):
+            init_test_distributed_environment(
+                tp_size, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port
+            )
+            _check_initialization_fallback(config, device, rank)
+            assert msa.resolve_index_k_shard(config, 4, "fp8", 16) == tp_size
+            comm = msa.get_comm()
+            assert comm is not None
+            assert msa._GATHER is not None
+            _check_indexer_forwards(config, device, rank, comm)
+        get_tp_group().barrier()
+
+
+def _check_initialization_fallback(config, device, rank):
+    import torch.distributed._symmetric_memory as symm_mem
+
+    from vllm.models.minimax_m3.nvidia import indexer_msa as msa
+    from vllm.models.minimax_m3.nvidia.ops.index_k_gather import (
+        _index_k_pull_pages_kernel,
+    )
+
+    original_empty = symm_mem.empty
+    for failure in ("recv_allocation", "gather_allocation", "gather_compile"):
+        with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as m:
+            m.setattr(msa, "_COMM", None)
+            m.setattr(msa, "_COMM_FAILED", False)
+            m.setattr(msa, "_GATHER", None)
+            injected = False
+
+            def fail_allocation(*args, failure=failure, **kwargs):
+                nonlocal injected
+                shape = args[0]
+                if (failure == "recv_allocation" and len(shape) == 5) or (
+                    failure == "gather_allocation" and len(shape) == 1
+                ):
+                    injected = True
+                    raise RuntimeError("injected indexer allocation failure")
+                return original_empty(*args, **kwargs)
+
+            def fail_compile(*args, **kwargs):
+                nonlocal injected
+                injected = True
+                raise RuntimeError("injected indexer compilation failure")
+
+            if rank == 1:
+                if failure == "gather_compile":
+                    m.setattr(_index_k_pull_pages_kernel, "warmup", fail_compile)
+                else:
+                    m.setattr(symm_mem, "empty", fail_allocation)
+
+            # A rank stranded in rendezvous or GPU polling cannot raise a Python
+            # timeout. Exit that worker so Ray reports failure and stops peers.
+            faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(90, exit=True)
+            try:
+                shard = msa.resolve_index_k_shard(config, 4, "fp8", 16)
+                assert injected == (rank == 1)
+                assert msa._GATHER is None
+                if failure == "recv_allocation":
+                    assert shard == 1
+                    assert msa.get_comm() is None
+                    assert msa._COMM_FAILED
+                else:
+                    assert shard == 4
+                    assert msa.get_comm() is not None
+                    local = torch.full(
+                        (1, 32, 128), rank, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device
+                    )
+                    pages = torch.tensor([0], device=device)
+                    full = msa.gather_prefill_pages(local, pages)
+                    expected = torch.arange(128, device=device) % 4
+                    assert torch.equal(full[0, :, 0].long(), expected)
+            finally:
+                faulthandler.cancel_dump_traceback_later()
+
+
+def _check_indexer_forwards(config, device, rank, comm):
+    from vllm.models.minimax_m3.nvidia import indexer_msa as msa
+
+    torch.manual_seed(123)
+    # Five layers exercise all three receive slot sets, including wrap across
+    # steps. Keep the actual production communication objects and dispatch.
+    layers = []
+    for sharded in (False, True):
+        layers.append(
+            [
+                msa.MiniMaxM3IndexerMSAImpl(
+                    num_kv_heads=1,
+                    scale=128**-0.5,
+                    topk_blocks=16,
+                    sparse_block_size=128,
+                    num_index_heads=1,
+                    index_head_dim=128,
+                    init_blocks=1,
+                    local_blocks=1,
+                    prefix=f"indexer_{sharded}_{layer}",
+                    cache_config=config.cache_config,
+                    indexer_kv_dtype="fp8",
+                    index_k_shard=4 if sharded else 1,
+                    topk_indices_buffer=torch.empty(
+                        (256, 1, 16), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+                    ),
+                )
+                for layer in range(5)
+            ]
+        )
+    builders = [
+        msa.MiniMaxM3IndexerMSAMetadataBuilder(
+            impls[0].index_cache.get_kv_cache_spec(config),
+            [impl.index_cache.prefix for impl in impls],
+            config,
+            device,
+        )
+        for impls in layers
+    ]
+
+    def run(sharded, metadata, queries):
+        impls = layers[sharded]
+        md = {impl.index_cache.prefix: metadata[sharded] for impl in impls}
+        with set_forward_context(md, config):
+            for impl, query in zip(impls, queries):
+                impl(query if sharded else query[:, rank : rank + 1].contiguous())
+
+    def check(metadata, queries, num_tokens):
+        run(False, metadata, queries)
+        for reference, sharded in zip(*layers):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                sharded.topk_indices_buffer[:num_tokens].sort(dim=-1).values,
+                reference.topk_indices_buffer[:num_tokens].sort(dim=-1).values,
+                rtol=0,
+                atol=0,
+            )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            metadata[1].unified_scores,
+            metadata[0].unified_scores,
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+        assert comm.errors.item() == 0
+
+    batches = [
+        BatchSpec(seq_lens=[129, 2305], query_lens=[1, 1]),
+        BatchSpec(seq_lens=[128, 2306], query_lens=[4, 4]),
+        BatchSpec(seq_lens=[128, 2307], query_lens=[8, 8]),
+        BatchSpec(seq_lens=[2305, 2561, 2624, 2720], query_lens=[1, 1, 64, 96]),
+    ]
+    for batch in batches:
+        common = create_common_attn_metadata(
+            batch, 128, device, arange_block_indices=True
+        )
+        num_pages = common.block_table_tensor.numel()
+        common.block_table_tensor = torch.randperm(num_pages, device=device)[
+            common.block_table_tensor.long()
+        ].int()
+        if batch.query_lens[-1] > 8:
+            # The two prefill requests share prefix pages, which the sharded
+            # builder must deduplicate and remap before the score-only call.
+            common.block_table_tensor[-1, :8] = common.block_table_tensor[-2, :8]
+        common.positions = torch.cat(
+            [
+                torch.arange(s - q, s, device=device)
+                for s, q in zip(batch.seq_lens, batch.query_lens)
+            ]
+        )
+        num_tokens = batch.compute_num_tokens()
+        bits = torch.arange(7, device=device)
+        page_codes = (
+            (torch.arange(num_pages, device=device)[:, None] >> bits) & 1
+        ) * 64
+        head_codes = torch.tensor([0, 21, 42, 85], device=device)[:, None]
+        queries, caches = [], []
+        for layer, (reference, sharded) in enumerate(zip(*layers)):

+                                    rK_upper,
+                                    rQ_f16[None, k, n, 1],
+                                    rC[None, m, n],
+                                )
+
+                    cute.arch.mbarrier_arrive(tma_empty_mbar + tma_stage)
+
+                    tile = super_id * PAGES + warp_id
+                    # Page row i holds the block's token i * TP + rank.
+                    k_base = tile * BLOCK + rank
+
+                    # causal mask
+                    for q in cutlass.range_constexpr(Q_TILES):
+                        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(4):
+                            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+                                col = q * 8 + (lane_id % 4) * 2 + j
+                                q_local_pos = col % MAX_DQL
+                                q_pos = q_start + q_local_pos
+                                k_pos = k_base + (i * 8 + lane_id // 4) * TP
+                                rC[q * 8 + i * 2 + j] = (
+                                    rC[q * 8 + i * 2 + j]
+                                    if q_pos >= k_pos
+                                    else float("-inf")
+                                )
+
+                    for q in cutlass.range_constexpr(Q_TILES):
+                        # thread-reduction along the page's 32 rows
+                        rScore = cute.make_rmem_tensor(2, Float32)
+                        rScore.fill(float("-inf"))
+                        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(4):
+                            rScore[0] = cute.arch.fmax(rScore[0], rC[i * 2 + 0 + q * 8])
+                            rScore[1] = cute.arch.fmax(rScore[1], rC[i * 2 + 1 + q * 8])
+
+                        # warp-reduction among lanes 0,4,8,12,...
+                        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(3):
+                            offset = 4 << i
+                            other0 = cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(
+                                rScore[0], offset=offset, mask=-1, mask_and_clamp=31
+                            )
+                            other1 = cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(
+                                rScore[1], offset=offset, mask=-1, mask_and_clamp=31
+                            )
+                            rScore[0] = cute.arch.fmax(rScore[0], other0)
+                            rScore[1] = cute.arch.fmax(rScore[1], other1)
+
+                        # lanes 0..3 hold columns q * 8 + 2 * lane + {0, 1}
+                        if lane_id * 2 < MMA_N:
+                            epi_buffer[q * MMA_N + lane_id * 2 + 0, warp_id] = rScore[0]
+                            epi_buffer[q * MMA_N + lane_id * 2 + 1, warp_id] = rScore[1]
+                    cute.arch.barrier(barrier_id=self.BAR_MMA, number_of_threads=128)
+
+                    # Push four page maxima to the head owner; padded pages are -inf.
+                    if warp_id == 0 and lane_id < BLOCK_Q:
+                        head_id = lane_id // MAX_DQL
+                        q_local_pos = lane_id - head_id * MAX_DQL
+                        if q_local_pos < decode_query_len:
+                            t = batch_id * decode_query_len + q_local_pos
+                            dst = head_id // HPR
+                            slot = (buf * TP + rank) * HPR + head_id % HPR
+                            elem = (slot * t_max + t) * MAX_K_TILES + super_id * PAGES
+                            _store_relaxed_sys_v4_f32(
+                                recv_bases[dst] + Int64(elem) * 4,
+                                epi_buffer[lane_id, 0],
+                                epi_buffer[lane_id, 1],
+                                epi_buffer[lane_id, 2],
+                                epi_buffer[lane_id, 3],
+                            )
+
+                    tma_stage = (tma_stage + 1) % self.num_stages
+                    if tma_stage == 0:
+                        tma_parity ^= 1
+
+    @cache
+    @staticmethod
+    def compile(
+        num_heads: int,
+        max_decode_query_len: int,
+        split_k: int,
+        head_dim: int = 128,
+    ):
+        bs = cute.sym_int()
+        total_tokens = cute.sym_int()
+        dtype = Float8E4M3FN
+
+        q = make_fake_tensor(
+            dtype, (total_tokens, num_heads, head_dim), divisibility=16
+        )
+        k_cache = make_fake_tensor(
+            dtype, (cute.sym_int(), ROWS, head_dim), divisibility=16
+        )
+        block_table = make_fake_tensor(Int32, (bs, cute.sym_int()), divisibility=1)
+        recv_bases = make_fake_tensor(Int64, (SUPPORTED_TP,), divisibility=1)
+        seq_lens = make_fake_tensor(Int32, (bs,), divisibility=1)
+        kernel = IndexDecodeScoreShardedKernel(
+            num_heads,
+            max_decode_query_len,
+            split_k,
+            head_dim,
+        )
+        stream = cute.runtime.make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=True)
+        return cute.compile(
+            kernel,
+            q,
+            k_cache,
+            block_table,
+            recv_bases,
+            seq_lens,
+            Int32(0),
+            Int32(0),
+            Int32(1),
+            stream,
+            options="--enable-tvm-ffi",
+        )
+
+
+def minimax_m3_index_decode_score_sharded_cutedsl(
+    idx_q: torch.Tensor,
+    index_kv_shard: torch.Tensor,
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    rank: int,
+    decode_query_len: int,
+    max_decode_query_len: int,
+    recv_bases: torch.Tensor,
+    buf: int,
+    t_max: int,
+    split_k: int = DEFAULT_SPLIT_K,
+) -> None:
+    """Score all index heads over local keys and push maxima to head owners.
+
+    Local K row i holds token i * 4 + rank. Receive buffers have FP32 layout
+    [bufs, tp, heads_per_rank, t_max, MAX_K_TILES]. Writes cover the valid
+    blocks rounded up to four, with -inf for padding.
+    """
+    if idx_q.dtype != torch.float8_e4m3fn or index_kv_shard.dtype != idx_q.dtype:
+        raise TypeError("sharded index decode score supports FP8 E4M3 only")
+    total_tokens, num_heads, head_dim = idx_q.shape
+    batch = block_table.shape[0]
+    assert index_kv_shard.shape[1] == ROWS
+    assert total_tokens == batch * decode_query_len
+    assert 1 <= decode_query_len <= max_decode_query_len
+    assert num_heads * max_decode_query_len <= 32
+    assert 0 <= rank < SUPPORTED_TP and num_heads % SUPPORTED_TP == 0
+    assert total_tokens <= t_max
+    kernel = IndexDecodeScoreShardedKernel.compile(
+        num_heads,
+        max_decode_query_len,
+        split_k,
+        head_dim,
+    )
+    kernel(idx_q, index_kv_shard, block_table, recv_bases, seq_lens, rank, buf, t_max)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _index_k_max_reduce_kernel(
+    recv_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    out_stride_t,
+    out_stride_h,
+    seq_lens_ptr,
+    decode_query_len,
+    err_ptr,
+    recv_stride_src,
+    recv_stride_h,
+    recv_stride_t,
+    W: tl.constexpr,
+    HPR: tl.constexpr,
+    CHUNK: tl.constexpr,
+    SPIN: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    th = tl.program_id(0)
+    t = th // HPR
+    hh = th % HPR
+    # The score kernel pushes whole 4-tile super-tiles (-inf past the last
+    # block, which the unified buffer already holds there).
+    seq_len = tl.load(seq_lens_ptr + t // decode_query_len)
+    n_tiles = (seq_len + 511) // 512 * 4
+    start = tl.program_id(1) * CHUNK
+    if start < n_tiles:
+        offs = start + tl.arange(0, CHUNK)
+        mask = offs < n_tiles
+        row = recv_ptr + hh * recv_stride_h + t * recv_stride_t + offs
+        # Poll every source's slot until none holds the sentinel.
+        acc = tl.full([CHUNK], float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+        pending = tl.full([], 1, tl.int32)
+        spins = tl.full([], 0, tl.int32)
+        while (pending > 0) & (spins < SPIN):
+            acc = tl.full([CHUNK], float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+            missing = tl.zeros([CHUNK], dtype=tl.int32)
+            for p in tl.static_range(W):
+                bits = tl.load(
+                    row + p * recv_stride_src, mask=mask, other=0, volatile=True
+                )
+                missing += (bits == -1).to(tl.int32)
+                acc = tl.maximum(acc, bits.to(tl.float32, bitcast=True))
+            pending = tl.sum(missing, axis=0)
+            spins += 1
+        if pending > 0:
+            tl.atomic_add(err_ptr, 1)
+            tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+                "trap; mov.u32 $0, 0;", "=r", [], dtype=tl.int32, is_pure=False, pack=1
+            )
+        tl.store(out_ptr + t * out_stride_t + hh * out_stride_h + offs, acc, mask=mask)
+        for p in tl.static_range(W):
+            tl.store(
+                row + p * recv_stride_src,
+                tl.full([CHUNK], -1, tl.int32),
+                mask=mask,
+            )

+"""Stage and gather token-sharded index-K pages for prefill."""
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+
+# Runtime integers are not value-specialized: a new divisibility class would
+# otherwise JIT-compile mid-step on one rank while its peers wait in the pull.
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["kv_page_stride", "num_programs", "rank", "epoch"])
+def _index_k_stage_pages_kernel(
+    kv_ptr,
+    kv_page_stride,
+    pages_ptr,
+    stage_ptr,
+    counter_ptr,
+    num_programs,
+    flag_bases_ptr,
+    rank,
+    epoch,
+    W: tl.constexpr,
+    PAGE_WORDS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    p = tl.program_id(0)
+    page = tl.load(pages_ptr + p).to(tl.int64)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, PAGE_WORDS)
+    vals = tl.load(kv_ptr + page * kv_page_stride + offs)
+    tl.store(stage_ptr + p.to(tl.int64) * PAGE_WORDS + offs, vals)
+    # Every thread's rows are stored before this program counts itself done;
+    # the last one resets the counter and publishes the epoch to every rank.
+    tl.debug_barrier()
+    done = tl.atomic_add(counter_ptr, 1, sem="acq_rel", scope="sys")
+    if done == num_programs - 1:
+        tl.atomic_xchg(counter_ptr, 0, sem="relaxed", scope="gpu")
+        for r in tl.static_range(W):
+            peer = tl.load(flag_bases_ptr + r).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64))
+            tl.atomic_xchg(peer + rank, epoch, sem="release", scope="sys")
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["epoch", "stage_off"])
+def _index_k_pull_pages_kernel(
+    flags_ptr,
+    epoch,
+    stage_bases_ptr,
+    stage_off,
+    out_ptr,
+    W: tl.constexpr,
+    ROWS: tl.constexpr,
+    ROW_WORDS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    # No timeout: reading a peer's staging buffer before it publishes would
+    # return stale rows, so a stalled peer stalls this rank instead.
+    for r in tl.static_range(W):
+        seen = tl.atomic_add(flags_ptr + r, 0, sem="acquire", scope="sys")
+        while seen < epoch:
+            seen = tl.atomic_add(flags_ptr + r, 0, sem="acquire", scope="sys")
+    tl.debug_barrier()
+    p = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    j = tl.arange(0, ROWS * W)
+    i = j // W
+    src_rank = j % W
+    c = tl.arange(0, ROW_WORDS)
+    base = tl.load(stage_bases_ptr + src_rank).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int32))
+    row = stage_off + p * (ROWS * ROW_WORDS) + i * ROW_WORDS
+    vals = tl.load(base[:, None] + row[:, None] + c[None, :])
+    dst = out_ptr + p * (ROWS * W * ROW_WORDS) + j[:, None] * ROW_WORDS + c[None, :]
+    tl.store(dst, vals)
